item.research_question: Can microwave-synthesized FeCoNiMnCu high entropy alloy (HEA) coatings on SS-304 steel enhance surface hardness, thermostability, and tribo-corrosion resistance for use in solid oxide fuel-cell (SOFC) interconnects?
item.material_system: Fe20Co20Ni20Mn20Cu20 HEA coating on SS-304 stainless steel substrate
item.processing_route: Ball-milling of Fe, Co, Ni, Mn, Cu powders (20 wt% each) at 200 rpm with a 5:1 ball-to-powder ratio; preheating at 100°C for 24 h; microwave hybrid heating (MHH) using a multimode applicator at 900 W and 2.45 GHz with charcoal as a susceptor; thermal exposure in air for up to 10 weeks at 800 °C
item.test_conditions: Hardness measured via Vickers tester (ASTM E384); corrosion tested by immersion in 3.5 wt% NaCl for 120 h (ASTM G44); wear tested via pin-on-disc (ASTM G99) at 2 m/s sliding speed, 1000 m distance, and 15 N axial load; microstructure analyzed via SEM and XRD
key_findings: Average hardness increased from 210 HV (SS-304) to 325 HV (coated), representing a 54.76% improvement.
Corrosion weight loss of the 20% Fe 20% Co 20% Ni 20% Mn 20% Cu coating was 0.3004 mg after 120 h in 3.5 wt% NaCl.
A protective Cr2O3 layer and a high-entropy spinel coating of (Fe, Co, Ni, Mn, Cu)3O4 formed after thermal exposure at 800 °C for 10 weeks.
XRD analysis identified phases including Fe, FeNi3, Al2O3, NiCO, CuO, Mn2O3, (Fe,Co,Ni,Mn,Cu)3O4, and Cr2O3.
SEM images revealed a uniform cladding distribution with homogeneity in the interfacial layer.
The cladding demonstrated remarkable stability under thermal expansion studies, withstanding significant volume variations at elevated temperatures.
item.mechanism: The formation of harder phases (FeNi3, Al2O3, NiCO, CuO, Mn2O3) during microwave cladding contributes to raised hardness. During thermal exposure, alloy elements react with atmospheric oxygen to form protective Cr2O3 and (Fe, Co, Ni, Mn, Cu)3O4 layers, which act as barriers against further oxidation, corrosion, and wear.
item.limitations: Some cracks were observed between the cladding layer and substrate, attributed to differential cooling rates, residual stresses, and inadequate bonding.
item.future_work: Optimize microwave cladding parameters including temperature, metallic powder content, environmental conditions, irradiation duration, pre-heating time, separators, and susceptors to further enhance effectiveness.
quotes: The deposited steel with 20% Fe 20% Co 20% Ni 20% Mn 20% Cu high entropy alloy (HEA) was exposed to thermal-exposure in the air for up to 10 weeks at 800 °C.
The results have unveiled about 54.76% improvement in the 'hardness of SS-304 alloy' after the 'microwave cladding' with a mixture of 20% Fe 20% Co 20% Ni 20% Mn 20% Cu.

item.research_question: Can a microwave-synthesized Fe20Co20Ni20Mn20Cu20 high-entropy alloy coating enhance the surface hardness, wear resistance, corrosion resistance, and thermal stability of SS-304 steel for SOFC interconnect applications?
item.material_system: SS-304 steel substrate coated with a mixture of 20% Fe, 20% Co, 20% Ni, 20% Mn, and 20% Cu (Fe20Co20Ni20Mn20Cu20 HEA)
item.processing_route: Microwave cladding using microwave energy to deposit the HEA powder onto the SS-304 surface
test_conditions: Corrosion exposure: 3.5 wt.% NaCl media and air exposure for up to 10 weeks at 800 °C
Wear testing: Sliding speed of 2 m/s, sliding distance of 1000 m, and load of 15 N
Thermal expansion test: 1200 °C for 72 h duration in a muffle-furnace
key_findings: Hardness of SS-304 was raised by approximately 54.76% after coating.
Wear rate of the coated sample was measured at 0.0018 mm3/m.
Coefficient of friction for the coated steel was determined to be 0.2.
Corrosion loss was reduced after thermal exposure in air for up to 10 weeks at 800 °C.
Thermal expansion test showed only a 1 mm3 variation in volume after exposure to 1200 °C for 72 h.
Protective Cr2O3 layer and high-entropy spinel coating of (Fe,Co,Ni,Mn,Cu)3O4 formed after thermal exposure.
Harder phases including Fe, FeNi3, Al2O3, NiCO, CuO, Fe2O3, and Mn2O3 were observed after microwave cladding.
item.mechanism: The alloying components (Fe, Co, Ni, Mn, and Cu) serve as sacrificial anodes to shield the underlying steel and help form stable oxide scales. High-temperature exposure aids in the development of protective oxide scales that function as barriers to retard the diffusion of corrosive species. The enhanced hardness is attributed to the formation of distinct harder phases such as Fe, FeNi3, Al2O3, NiCO, CuO, Fe2O3, and Mn2O3.
item.limitations: The text notes that dark spots on the corroded surface indicate localized corrosion where the coating may have been breached or performed less well due to flaws or microstructural alterations. The study also implies that electrical conductivity and area-specific resistance were not fully characterized in this specific work.
item.future_work: Emphasis must be contemplated on analyzing the electrical-conductivity for SOFCs interconnects applications. Emphasis must be centered on analyzing the oxidation-resistance and area-specific resistance in simulated service environments. Additional characterizations must be contemplated on the coatings before and after thermal exposure in air at 800°C. The cross-section of the coatings has been assessed to affirm the continuous and protective (FeCoNiMnCu)3O4 coating.
quotes: The hardness has been ameliorated by about 54.76%.
The results revealed a minimal change in volume, with only a 1 mm3 variation observed
The development of protective oxide scales on the surface of SS-304 may be aided by the high temperature.
